raw: Act 2, Scene 5 — Capulet’s Garden

sentences.en: Capulet’s Garden

summary.en: Juliet waits impatiently for the Nurse. At last, the Nurse tells her to go to Friar Lawrence's cell to be married.
summary.ko: 줄리엣은 유모를 초조하게 기다린다. 마침내 유모는 줄리엣에게 로런스 신부의 수도실로 가서 결혼하라고 전한다.

raw: Enter Juliet.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
The clock struck nine when I did send the Nurse,
In half an hour she promised to return.
Perchance she cannot meet him. That’s not so.
O, she is lame. Love’s heralds should be thoughts,
Which ten times faster glides than the sun’s beams,
Driving back shadows over lowering hills:
Therefore do nimble-pinion’d doves draw love,
And therefore hath the wind-swift Cupid wings.
Now is the sun upon the highmost hill
Of this day’s journey, and from nine till twelve
Is three long hours, yet she is not come.
Had she affections and warm youthful blood,
She’d be as swift in motion as a ball;
My words would bandy her to my sweet love,
And his to me.
But old folks, many feign as they were dead;
Unwieldy, slow, heavy and pale as lead.

sentences.en: The clock struck nine when I sent the Nurse, and she promised to return in half an hour.
sentences.ko: 시계가 아홉 시를 칠 때 유모를 보냈는데, 반 시간이면 돌아온다고 했다.

sentences.en: Maybe she cannot meet him, but that is not true.
sentences.ko: 어쩌면 그이를 못 만났는지도 모른다. 아니, 그럴 리 없다.

sentences.en: She is so slow.
Thoughts of love should be the messengers because they move ten times faster than the sun's rays.
sentences.ko: 사랑의 전령은 생각이어야 한다. 햇살보다 열 배는 빠르니까.

sentences.en: They drive back shadows over low hills.
sentences.ko: 그것들은 낮은 언덕 위로 그림자를 몰아낸다.

sentences.en: That is why quick-winged doves pull love's chariot and why the wind-swift Cupid has wings.
sentences.ko: 그래서 날개 달린 비둘기가 사랑의 마차를 끌고, 바람처럼 빠른 큐피드에게 날개가 있는 것이다.

sentences.en: Now the sun is on the highest hill of this day's journey.
sentences.ko: 이제 태양은 오늘 여정에서 가장 높은 언덕에 와 있다.

sentences.en: From nine until twelve are three long hours, yet she has not come.
sentences.ko: 아홉 시부터 열두 시까지는 세 시간이나 되는 긴 시간이지만, 그녀는 아직 오지 않았다.

sentences.en: If she had feelings and warm young blood, she would be as fast as a ball.
sentences.ko: 유모에게 사랑하는 마음과 뜨거운 젊은 피가 있다면 공처럼 빨리 오갈 텐데.

sentences.en: My words would carry her to my sweet love, and his words would come to me.
sentences.ko: 내 말은 나의 사랑에게 전달되고, 그의 말도 나에게 전해질 텐데.

sentences.en: But many old people act as if they were already dead.
sentences.ko: 하지만 많은 노인들은 이미 죽은 것처럼 행동한다.

sentences.en: They are clumsy, slow, heavy, and pale like lead.
sentences.ko: 그들은 서투르고 느리고 무거우며 납처럼 창백하다.

raw: Enter Nurse and Peter.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O God, she comes. O honey Nurse, what news?
Hast thou met with him? Send thy man away.

sentences.en: Oh God, she comes.
Oh dear Nurse, what news? Have you met him?
sentences.ko: 오, 유모, 무슨 소식이야? 그를 만났니?

sentences.en: Send your man away.

speaker: NURSE
raw: Peter, stay at the gate.

sentences.en: Peter, stay at the gate.

raw: Exit Peter.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Now, good sweet Nurse,—O Lord, why look’st thou sad?
Though news be sad, yet tell them merrily;
If good, thou sham’st the music of sweet news
By playing it to me with so sour a face.

sentences.en: Now, good sweet Nurse.
Oh Lord, why do you look sad?
sentences.ko: 오 주여, 왜 그렇게 슬픈 표정을 짓고 있어?

sentences.en: Even if the news is sad, tell it happily.
If it is good news, you ruin the music of the news.
sentences.ko: 좋은 소식이라면, 그렇게 말하면 좋은 소식의 음악을 망치는 거야.

sentences.en: You are playing it to me with such a sour face.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
I am aweary, give me leave awhile;
Fie, how my bones ache! What a jaunt have I had!

sentences.en: I am tired, so leave me alone for a moment.
sentences.ko: 나 지쳤어, 잠깐만 쉬게 해 줘.

sentences.en: Ugh, how my bones ache! What a long trip I have had!
sentences.ko: 아이고, 뼈마디야! 정말 먼 길을 다녀왔구나!

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I would thou hadst my bones, and I thy news:
Nay come, I pray thee speak; good, good Nurse, speak.

sentences.en: I wish you had my bones and I had your news.
sentences.ko: 네가 내 뼈를 가지고 내가 네 소식을 가졌으면 좋겠어.

sentences.en: Come on, please speak.
Good, good Nurse, speak.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Jesu, what haste? Can you not stay a while? Do you not see that I am
out of breath?

sentences.en: Jesus, why the hurry?
Can you not stay a while?
Do you not see that I am out of breath?
sentences.ko: 내가 숨이 턱까지 차오른 게 안 보이니?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
How art thou out of breath, when thou hast breath
To say to me that thou art out of breath?
The excuse that thou dost make in this delay
Is longer than the tale thou dost excuse.
Is thy news good or bad? Answer to that;
Say either, and I’ll stay the circumstance.
Let me be satisfied, is’t good or bad?

sentences.en: How are you out of breath?
You have enough breath to tell me that you are out of breath.
sentences.ko: 숨이 차다고 말할 기운은 충분히 있잖아.

sentences.en: The excuse you make for this delay is longer than the story you are telling.
sentences.ko: 지체하는 이유를 설명하는 말이 네가 하는 이야기보다 더 길어.

sentences.en: Is your news good or bad?
Answer that question.
Say either, and I will listen to the details.
sentences.ko: 둘 중 하나만 말해봐, 그럼 자세히 들어줄게.

sentences.en: Let me be satisfied, is it good or bad?
sentences.ko: 내 궁금증부터 풀어줘, 좋은 거야, 나쁜 거야?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Well, you have made a simple choice; you know not how to choose a man.
Romeo? No, not he. Though his face be better than any man’s, yet his
leg excels all men’s, and for a hand and a foot, and a body, though
they be not to be talked on, yet they are past compare. He is not the
flower of courtesy, but I’ll warrant him as gentle as a lamb. Go thy
ways, wench, serve God. What, have you dined at home?

sentences.en: Well, you made a foolish choice.
You do not know how to choose a man.
Romeo? No, not him.
His face is better than any man's face.
sentences.ko: 그의 얼굴은 그 어떤 남자보다도 훌륭해.

sentences.en: His leg is better than all men's legs.
sentences.ko: 그의 다리도 모든 남자의 다리보다 멋지단다.

sentences.en: His hands and feet are also very good.
They are nothing special to talk about, but still they are the best.
sentences.ko: 딱히 입에 올릴 만한 건 아니지만, 그래도 비길 데가 없어.

sentences.en: He is not the best at being polite.
But I promise he is as gentle as a lamb.
sentences.ko: 하지만 약속컨대 그는 어린 양처럼 온순해.

sentences.en: Go your way, girl, and serve God.
sentences.ko: 네 갈 길 가거라, 얘야. 하나님을 잘 섬기고.

sentences.en: What, did you eat at home?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
No, no. But all this did I know before.
What says he of our marriage? What of that?

sentences.en: No, no.
I knew all of this before.
sentences.ko: 난 이미 이 모든 걸 알고 있었어.

sentences.en: What does he say about our marriage?
sentences.ko: 그가 우리 결혼에 대해 뭐라고 말했어?

sentences.en: What about that?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Lord, how my head aches! What a head have I!
It beats as it would fall in twenty pieces.
My back o’ t’other side,—O my back, my back!
Beshrew your heart for sending me about
To catch my death with jauncing up and down.

sentences.en: Lord, how my head aches!
What a head I have!
It feels like it will fall into twenty pieces.
And my back, on the other side!
Oh, my back, my back!
May your heart be cursed for sending me running up and down until I nearly died!
sentences.ko: 나를 죽을 정도로 이리저리 뛰어다니게 만든 네 마음이 저주받기를!

speaker: JULIET
raw:
I’faith, I am sorry that thou art not well.
Sweet, sweet, sweet Nurse, tell me, what says my love?

sentences.en: I am sorry that you are not well.
Sweet, sweet, sweet Nurse, tell me.
What does my love say?

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Your love says like an honest gentleman,
And a courteous, and a kind, and a handsome,
And I warrant a virtuous,—Where is your mother?

sentences.en: Your love speaks like an honest gentleman who is courteous, kind, and handsome.
sentences.ko: 네 사랑은 예의 바르고 친절하며 잘생긴 신사처럼 말해.

sentences.en: I promise he is virtuous.
Where is your mother?

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Where is my mother? Why, she is within.
Where should she be? How oddly thou repliest.
‘Your love says, like an honest gentleman,
‘Where is your mother?’

sentences.en: Where is my mother?
She is inside.
Where else would she be?
You answered very strangely.
'Your love says, like an honest gentleman, where is your mother?'
sentences.ko: '네 사랑이 정직한 신사답게 말하길, 네 어머니는 어디 계시냐?'라니.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
O God’s lady dear,
Are you so hot? Marry, come up, I trow.
Is this the poultice for my aching bones?
Henceforward do your messages yourself.

sentences.en: Oh, Holy Mary! Are you so impatient?
Well, well, calm down!
Is this the cure for my aching bones?
sentences.ko: 이게 내 아픈 뼈를 고쳐줄 약이라도 되는 줄 아니?

sentences.en: From now on, deliver your messages yourself.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Here’s such a coil. Come, what says Romeo?

sentences.en: This is such a mess.
Come, what does Romeo say?

speaker: NURSE
raw: Have you got leave to go to shrift today?

sentences.en: Do you have permission to go to confession today?

speaker: JULIET
raw: I have.

sentences.en: I have.

speaker: NURSE
raw:
Then hie you hence to Friar Lawrence’ cell;
There stays a husband to make you a wife.
Now comes the wanton blood up in your cheeks,
They’ll be in scarlet straight at any news.
Hie you to church. I must another way,
To fetch a ladder by the which your love
Must climb a bird’s nest soon when it is dark.
I am the drudge, and toil in your delight;
But you shall bear the burden soon at night.
Go. I’ll to dinner; hie you to the cell.

sentences.en: Then hurry away to Friar Lawrence's small room where a husband waits to make you a wife.
sentences.ko: 그럼 서둘러 로런스 신부님의 수도실로 가렴. 거기서 신랑이 너를 신부로 맞으려 기다리고 있어.

sentences.en: Now the excited blood rushes to your cheeks and they will turn red at any news.
sentences.ko: 이제 설레는 피가 네 뺨으로 몰려와 어떤 소식에도 얼굴이 붉어질 거야.

sentences.en: Hurry to the church while I go another way to get a ladder.
sentences.ko: 나는 사다리를 가지러 다른 길로 갈 테니 너는 서둘러 성당으로 가라.

sentences.en: Your love will use it to climb up to your bird's nest when it is dark.
sentences.ko: 어두워지면 네 사랑이 그걸 타고 네 새 둥지로 올라올 거야.

sentences.en: I am the servant who works for your pleasure, but tonight you will carry the weight.
sentences.ko: 나는 네 기쁨을 위해 고생하는 하녀지만, 오늘 밤엔 네가 그 무게를 짊어지겠지.

sentences.en: Go! I will go to dinner, and you must hurry to the cell.
sentences.ko: 어서 가! 나는 저녁 먹으러 간다. 너는 어서 수도실로 가거라.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Hie to high fortune! Honest Nurse, farewell.

sentences.en: Hurry to high fortune!
Honest Nurse, goodbye.

raw: Exeunt.
